title: Almost-linear directed vertex connectivity
formal: Is there a uniform bounded-error randomized word-RAM algorithm computing the exact vertex connectivity and an attaining vertex separator of every simple unweighted directed graph in \((m+n)^{1+o(1)}\) worst-case time?
definitions: The graph is given by its vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge2\), and an explicit list of \(m\) arcs. It has no loops and at most one arc per ordered pair; opposite arcs are allowed. For \(S\subseteq V\), remove \(S\) and all incident arcs. Define \(\kappa(G)\) as the smallest \(|S|\) for which the remainder is not strongly connected or contains at most one vertex. Strong connectivity means reachability for every ordered pair of remaining vertices. Thus an input that is not strongly connected has value zero, and a complete bidirected graph has value \(n-1\). Output the value and an attaining \(S\). Whenever at least two vertices remain, failure of strong connectivity is equivalent to a partition \((L,S,R)\) with nonempty \(L,R\) and no arc from \(L\) to \(R\). Use a uniform word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_{2}(n+2)\rceil\), for a fixed positive integer \(d\) chosen with the algorithm and large enough for its addresses and input values. Unit-cost instructions are word reads/writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), and integer quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Multiword computation is charged by its component instructions. The fixed finite program receives no advice or precomputed tables; all initialization, preprocessing and output writes count. Randomness consists of independent uniform random words, each generated at unit cost. On every input, the whole output must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). The time bound holds for every random execution, including unsuccessful ones. Write \(N=m+n\). Almost-linear time means that there exist one algorithm, a constant \(C\) and a function \(h:\mathbb{N}\to[1,\infty)\), independent of the input graph, with \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\log h(N)/\log N=0\), such that the time is at most \(CNh(N)\) for every input. All hidden constants are independent of the graph.

context_blocks.text: Directed vertex connectivity measures resilience to vertex failures when communication is asymmetric. A single removed vertex can affect many arcs simultaneously.
Chuzhoy, Mosenzon and Trabelsi give randomized unweighted time \(\min\{m^{1+o(1)}\kappa,n^{2+o(1)}\}\). Their weighted result also improves the longstanding Henzinger–Rao–Gabow bound.
These bounds cover important sparse-connectivity and dense-graph regimes. The question requires an almost-linear bound for every density and connectivity, while allowing randomization.
Almost-linear relative approximation schemes are known, but their precision cost does not establish the general exact endpoint.

why: A uniform almost-linear algorithm would settle the remaining general exact running-time gap for directed vertex robustness, a classical network problem.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

status_note: Sources and subsequent-result searches checked on 13 September 2026. sentences: Directed vertex connectivity measures the smallest vertex failure set destroying strong connectivity or leaving at most one vertex.
The task is to output its exact value and a minimum separator in an unweighted digraph.
The question asks for a bounded-error randomized algorithm with almost-linear worst-case time.
The reviewed algorithms cover important density and connectivity regimes but leave a general gap.
The target demands one bound valid for every directed input graph.
